items.title: Orrin Keepnews — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He gave me, what I later came to recognize as a typical Miles Davis withering glare and he said, “I should recommend somebody to him?”

ctx.x: Into Riverside, or Prestige? He came to your office?

He came in. What happened was, Weinstock had come…our office, I don’t really remember why…we were on West 48th street, and Prestige was on West 50th street. Miles was curious. Where was Weinstock going in the name of them? Really curious when he saw where he was going, so he walked in moments afterwards. So, we got involved in a conversation in which I said…I got it now. We had some recent albums on the wall, including a couple of Randy Weston. I had, no, I look around and saw that Miles was looking at these…
compulsions? These were the people that I was living with! They were doing what they felt they had to do! I’m the same story.

items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Miles Davis, who I never worked with but who I knew pretty well over a very long period of time

ctx.x: He was listening to Sonny Rollins with Thelonious Monk, “The Way You Look Tonight,” and he says, “I don’t see how a record company can record something like that. You know the way Monk plays he never gives any support to a rhythm section. When I had him on my date I had him lay out.” You know, has there been circumstances—

Oh come on he had him lay out on one tune, the whole celebrated story, as Monk has said, there never was any danger of there being a fight because I would have killed him. And he’s right. Despite all the photos of Miles in boxing gear. Miles, this is a whole other subject but you brought Miles into it. Miles Davis, who I never worked with but who I knew pretty well over a very long period of time, and basically I’m going to say just in the whole pantheon of things, not that he ever asked me to but I approve of…

demanded to be the centerpiece, to be the focal point of what was going on, to be in control, coming head to head, actually it is a wonder that they didn’t really start duking it out together. But Monk said they didn’t because he would have killed him. But anyway you must — particularly when you’re dealing with famous remarks and famous incidents, try to look behind the surface as much as you can.
